summary: The 200K cameraman clip (6,810 views) remains 5-10x ahead of everything else and its formula is now fully confirmed: a specific surprising number or quotable phrase locked into a colored top-bar text banner in the first frame, the spoken punchline echoed as 2-3 word ALL-CAPS subtitles, blur-fill framing, and total runtime under 25 seconds. The 1,150-1,440 view cluster all share one of three angles — an absurd celebrity/cultural hot take Cartier defends with a straight face, a physical or social moment with a stranger, or a self-aware fumble Cartier catches mid-sentence. Titles that open with a concrete detail (a number, a quoted phrase, a named situation) consistently beat vague titles by 3-5x. moments_to_pick: Cartier says a specific number out loud — a salary, price, count, year, or stat — that will stun a first-time viewer with zero prior context
Cartier delivers a confident, slightly absurd hot take about a celebrity, a show, food, a job or a game and defends it with a straight face for at least 5 seconds
An unscripted exchange with a stranger turns physical or competitive — a skill demo, a challenge accepted, a compliment that backfires
Cartier catches himself mid-rant or mid-claim and self-corrects with visible embarrassment — the self-aware fumble is the whole clip
Chat says something that triggers a full-second Cartier silence followed by audible laughter — the delayed reaction IS the punchline
A social moment where someone in the stream says something unexpectedly bold and Cartier's face does the work before he speaks

title_formula: Open with the specific surprising detail — a number, a direct quote fragment, or a named situation — in plain English. Follow with the reaction or consequence in 3-6 words. Close with one emoji. Never start the title with 'Cartier2Real' as the first word — lead with the detail. Never use currency sy
caption_formula: Line 1: One punchy reaction sentence that rewords the hook from the audience's point of view — do not copy the title word for word. Line 2: One sentence teasing what Cartier said or did next without fully spoiling the payoff. Line 3: 'Catch Cartier live on Kick: kick.com/cartier2real' with @cartier2
avoid: Any establishing shot, slow pan, or silent lead-in — cut directly to the moment or the spoken word on frame one, no exceptions
Clips over 25 seconds unless a physical or social arc is genuinely impossible to understand without the build — absolute hard cap 35s per campaign rules
Vague titles with no concrete detail: 'Cartier reacts to something wild' names nothing — always lead with the specific thing
Currency symbols anywhere in titles, captions, or on-screen text — spell out numbers in words or use 'K' notation only
Moments where Cartier or anyone in the stream looks genuinely bad, embarrassed against their will, or disrespected — only pick moments where he's in on the joke or clearly winning
Repeating the same emoji in both the title and the top-bar hook banner — vary them so the two lines feel distinct
experiment: On one clip this cycle, test 2 words per caption instead of 3 — single-breath chunks like 'NO CAP' / 'TWO HUNDRED' / 'EVERY YEAR' force the eye to snap to each beat and may increase watch time on the strongest quotable lines. Keep everything else identical to the control style so the variable is iso
